grade.first_issue: The inference \(x\equiv54\pmod{60}\Rightarrow x\equiv6\pmod8\) is false, so the subsequent modulo \(17\) and modulo \(73\) contradiction does not eliminate that branch.
grade.summary: The submission correctly finds both solutions and rigorously handles \(c=1\), but its proof of completeness fails. Several remaining branches are eliminated by invalid congruence deductions or unsupported assertions, including “the only solution” and “similar contradictions rule out” all larger \(s\).
strengths: Correctly proves \(a>c\), applies the \(2\)-adic valuation formula, and obtains \((3,1,1)\) and \((6,2,4)\).

errors.description: The false reduction from a congruence modulo \(60\) to one modulo \(8\) invalidates a load-bearing contradiction.
In the \(y\equiv2\pmod{12}\) branch, one residue case is not treated and the claimed uniqueness of \((x,y)=(6,2)\) is merely asserted.
For even \(j\), only \(s=3\) is partially considered; the growth argument is unjustified and all cases \(s=6,9,\ldots\) are dismissed without proof.
